blocks.prompt: 2. Differentiate with respect to the variable involved: \(y = x^2 \cos x\)
blocks.explanation:
Sab se pehle dekhte hain ke \(y\) kis qisam ka function hai: \(x^2\) aur \(\cos x\) aapas mein multiply ho rahe hain, yani product hai.
Diya kya hai? \(y = x^2\cos x\). Variable \(x\) hai, to humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) chahiye.
Rule kaunsa? Product rule, kyunke jab do functions multiply hon to har ek ka derivative baari baari lena parta hai.
Plan: product rule lagayenge, derivatives rakhenge, aur aakhir mein \(x\) common nikal kar jawab saaf karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = x^2\cos x\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: product rule \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\), jahan \(u = x^2\) aur \(v = \cos x\). Product rule ko aise yaad rakhein: pehle ka derivative darja doosra, plus pehla darja doosre ka derivative.

Product rule lagayein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x^2)'\cos x + x^2(\cos x)'\]
Kyun: ek waqt mein ek hi factor ka derivative lete hain aur doosre ko waisa hi rehne dete hain. Phir dono hisse jama karte hain.
Dhyan dein: \((x^2\cos x)'\) ko \((x^2)'(\cos x)' = 2x(-\sin x)\) likhna bohat aam ghalti hai. Product ka derivative derivatives ka product nahi hota.

Derivatives rakhein
\[= 2x\cos x + x^2(-\sin x)\]
\[= 2x\cos x - x^2\sin x\]
Kyun: power rule se \((x^2)' = 2x\), aur \((\cos x)' = -\sin x\). Plus aur minus mil kar minus bana.

Common nikalein
\[= x(2\cos x - x\sin x)\]
Kyun: dono terms mein \(x\) maujood hai, to usay bahar nikal kar jawab chhota aur saaf ho gaya. Yeh zaroori nahi, lekin achha jawab aisa hi dikhta hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \pi:\ 2\pi(-1) - \pi^2(0) = -2\pi\]
Kyun: \(x = \pi\) ke aas paas \(\cos x\) taqreeban \(-1\) hai, to function taqreeban \(-x^2\) jaisa hai, jis ka slope \(-2x = -2\pi\) hai. Hamara formula bhi yahi de raha hai, is liye jawab theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\cos x - x^2\sin x = x(2\cos x - x\sin x)\)
